item.message: `[features].use_legacy_landlock` is deprecated and will be removed soon. (Remove this setting to stop opting into the legacy Linux sandbox behavior.)

`[features].web_search_cached` is deprecated because web search is enabled by default. (Set `web_search` to `"live"`, `"indexed"`, `"cached"`, or `"disabled"` at the top level (or under a profile) in config.toml if you want to override it.)

item.text: {"verdict":"request_changes","summary":"The image identity, credential brokering, live-evidence bootstrap, tmpfs verdict retrieval, runtime-qualified mount allowance, and JCS clarifications remain addressed. However, the invocation fingerprint still omits security-critical settings, and the retained-wrapper lifecycle is not bounded if the runner crashes. Two additional robustness gaps remain.","recommendations":[{"severity":"blocking","location":"Premises / live-evidence — container_invocation_profile_hash","issue":"[P1] The enumerated semantic profile omits several settings on which the boundary depends: the non-root UID/GID, read-only rootfs, no-new-privileges, exact Codex argv flags other than `--disable`, environment allowlist, published ports, resource limits, and attachment/control behavior. Evidence can therefore remain current after one of these protections is weakened or removed. This means the earlier invocation-fingerprint finding is not fully addressed.","suggestion":"Canonicalize and hash every security-relevant effective setting, including the complete Codex argv template with typed dynamic values, UID/GID, rootfs mode, security options, environment, port mappings, resource limits, mounts, stream attachment, runtime server/backend identity, and wrapper protocol. Derive or cross-check the record against runtime inspection, and test that changing each field invalidates evidence."},{"severity":"blocking","location":"Architecture: container lifecycle and verdict retrieval; Credential lifecycle","issue":"[P1] The wrapper intentionally remains alive until the host releases it, while the timeout and cleanup are enforced only by the runner. If the runner is killed, crashes, or loses its daemon connection, the container can run or wait forever, retaining the credential bind and preventing safe stale-directory recovery. Thus the claimed bounded run and guaranteed cleanup do not hold for a predictable failure mode.","suggestion":"Add an in-container watchdog that kills Codex and exits the wrapper after an absolute deadline independently of the host client. Label containers with narrowly scoped ownership/run identifiers, reap verified stale containers on startup, and remove a stale staging directory only after confirming that no owned live container references it."},{"severity":"important","location":"Container lifecycle, step 3","issue":"[P2] Direct stdout/stderr and JSONL capture has no stated per-stream or aggregate byte bound. A long or malformed run can exhaust host memory or disk despite container memory limits, regressing the previously requested bounded-stream lifecycle.","suggestion":"Use streaming parsing and online secret scanning with explicit per-channel and aggregate limits, bounded diagnostic retention, and immediate container termination when a limit is exceeded. Apply bounded reads to copied verdict/status artifacts as well, and test over-limit behavior."},{"severity":"important","location":"The credential — host-side broker; Risks and mitigations — token lifetime","issue":"[P2] “Valid” or “fresh” at launch does not ensure that the token outlives the configured round. No minimum remaining lifetime, clock-skew margin, or relationship between token expiry and the maximum wrapper deadline is defined.","suggestion":"Require verified remaining lifetime of at least the maximum round deadline plus startup and clock-skew margins before container creation. Refresh or mint again when below that threshold, and fail before launch if the provider cannot supply a sufficiently long-lived access-only token."}]}
